title: Implement aisle bucketing and stable aggregate ordering
description: Implement `ShoppingList.aggregate(recipes:aisleConfig:)` to flatten recipe ingredients, canonicalise names, group items by aisle, preserve first-occurrence ordering within buckets, and append the unmatched `Other` bucket last.
acceptance_criteria: `ShoppingList.aggregate(recipes:aisleConfig:)` is added as a static pure function in `Aggregation.swift`.
When `aisleConfig` is present, ingredients are assigned to aisle buckets using alias-aware lookup and canonical names come from the matched aisle item.
When `aisleConfig` is absent or no aisle match exists, ingredients are normalised with lowercased trimmed names and grouped under `name == nil`.
Aisle ordering follows `aisleConfig.sections` order, with the nil `Other` bucket appended last only when needed.
Items within each bucket retain stable first-occurrence order across the input recipe list.
Only recipe ingredients participate; cookware, timers, notes, formatting, and I/O remain out of scope.

handoff_summary.completed: - Added `public extension ShoppingList` block in `Aggregation.swift` containing `aggregate(recipes:aisleConfig:)` static pure function and a private `mergeQuantity(_:into:)` helper. - All six acceptance criteria satisfied: aisle bucketing with alias-aware lookup, canonical names from config, nil fallback for unmatched/no-config, sections-order aisle ordering, stable first-occurrence item ordering within buckets, and ingredient-only scope. - Build passes clean (`Build complete!`).
handoff_summary.remaining: Tester agent should write tests covering: (1) no aisleConfig — all items in nil bucket, (2) full aisle match — items ordered by sections, (3) mixed match/miss — named aisles then nil bucket, (4) quantity merging — same-unit summed, different-unit separate, text appended, quantity-less items with empty quantities, (5) empty recipes — empty aisles array, (6) alias lookup — ingredient name resolves via AisleItem.aliases to canonical.
handoff_summary.risks: None significant. All referenced types (AisleConfig, AisleSection, AisleItem, Recipe, Ingredient, Quantity, ShoppingList) were already public in the module. The nested dictionary mutation pattern (copy-mutate-write-back) is safe but O(n) per ingredient; acceptable for recipe-scale lists.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester agent should write unit tests for `ShoppingList.aggregate` covering the scenarios listed in `remaining`.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: No conflicts expected. This bead only appended to `Aggregation.swift`; no other bead in this feature tree modifies that file.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: Placed the extension on `ShoppingList` (rather than as a free function or on `AggregatedShoppingList`) to match the `ShoppingList.aggregate(...)` call-site implied by the bead spec. Ordered aisle output strictly by `aisleConfig.sections` rather than by first-encounter order, which means any named aisle that arose during ingredient processing but is not in `sections` would be silently dropped — this cannot happen because `aisle(for:)` only returns sections that exist in `sections`. Used copy-mutate-write-back for nested dictionary mutation to avoid Swift's `inout` restriction on computed subscripts.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: No tests written (developer scope). Tester agent should cover: nil config, full-match, partial-match, quantity merge rules (same-unit sum, different-unit append, text append, quantity-less), empty input, stable ordering, alias resolution.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: The inner aisle-item lookup uses `Array.contains` (O(n) per ingredient). For recipe-scale data this is fine; if ingredient counts grow large a Set-based index could be added.

conflict_risks: No conflicts expected. This bead only appended to `Aggregation.swift`; no other bead in this feature tree modifies that file.

execution_history.summary: Implemented `ShoppingList.aggregate(recipes:aisleConfig:)` as a public static function in `Aggregation.swift`. The function flattens recipe ingredients, performs alias-aware aisle lookup via `AisleConfig.aisle(for:)` and `AisleConfig.canonical(for:)`, deduplicates by canonical name, accumulates quantities (summing same-unit numerics, appending text and different-unit quantities), orders aisles by `aisleConfig.sections` order, and appends the nil "Other" bucket last only when needed.
